issues.title: Define a shared alert lifecycle and actionable UI contract
issues.review_trigger: Review before publishing a CLI/API or whenever a new source cannot express its native action semantics.

issues.title: Add validated TOML configuration and explicit source/calendar selection
issues.review_trigger: Review when a provider changes identities or a configuration default could expand interruption scope.

issues.title: Make alert state reliable across concurrency, restart and suspend/resume
issues.review_trigger: Review after any lost reminder, duplicate action, stale replay or scheduler-ownership change.

issues.title: Isolate the EDS source adapter and reconcile native and fallback reminders
issues.review_trigger: Review after any native/fallback overlap, recurring-instance mismatch or account reconnect.

issues.title: Expose an opt-in local CLI/JSON interface for external alert producers
issues.review_trigger: Review before treating an example producer as a supported adapter or freezing the external protocol.

issues.title: Support the shared large overlay on COSMIC, Hyprland and KDE Wayland
issues.review_trigger: Review on any compositor/library upgrade, focus/stacking failure or monitor topology change.

issues.title: Establish GNOME Wayland display support with a shared-UI feasibility gate
issues.review_trigger: Review at the shared-UI experiment result and each supported GNOME release boundary.

issues.title: Add configurable audible alerts tied to the visible reminder lifecycle
issues.review_trigger: Review on a playback leak, competing alert, failed device or changed interruption policy.

issues.title: Discovery: establish the native KDE/Akonadi calendar adapter boundary
issues.review_trigger: Review when the evidence is available, the adapter would require a sync-engine rewrite or a user needs unsupported capabilities.

issues.title: Ship repeatable user-service installation, migration and diagnostics
issues.review_trigger: Review before publishing installation instructions, changing names/dependencies or expanding desktop-support claims.
